title: Searching simple biomarkers to phenotype type 2 diabetic patients and personalize their treatment
official: Searching simple biomarkers to phenotype type 2 diabetic patients and personalize their treatment
summary: Main objective: To assess responses to different glucose-lowering treatments - dapagliflozin vs oral semaglutide - in patients with T2D categorized into 2 groups, depending on their prevalent insulin resistance (IR) or prevalent insulin secretion deficit (ISD). The differential responses to therapy will be monitored usig a series of non-canonical (e.g., adiponectin, irisin, serpin B1) or canonical biomarkers (HbA1c, glucagon, GLP-1, GIP, insulin, proinflammatory mediators) or other metabolites potentially detected in metabo-lipidomic analysis
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Provision of informed consent prior to any study specific procedures
2. Will and ability to comply with the protocol
3. Age: 20 – 80 years old
4. Sex: Males and Females
5. Stable therapy with metformin for at least 6 months
6. Suboptimal glycemic control (HbA1c ≥6.5 %)
7. Fasting C-peptide > 1 ng/mL (0.33 nmol/L)
8. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative blood or urine pregnancy test at the baseline visit
9. Female subjects of childbearing potential must be willing to use an adequate method of contraception as outlined in Section 5.9 of the protocol
10. Ability to take oral medications
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous type 1 diabetes or Late-Onset Autoimmune Diabetes of the Adult (LADA) diagnosis, as assessed by medical history
2. Severe liver dysfunction
3. history of pancreatitis, patients with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption
4. Severe renal dysfunction (eGFR < 25 ml/min/1.73m2)
5. Uncontrolled hypertension
6. Uncontrolled dyslipidemia (total cholesterol > 300 mg/dl and/or LDLc > 200 and/or triglycerides > 500 mg/dl)
7. Known hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients in study drug
8. Pregnant or breast-feeding women
9. Women of childbearing potential with either a positive or no pregnancy test at baseline. Postmenopausal women must have been amenorrhoeic for at least 12 months to be considered of nonchildbearing potential
10. Treatment with hormonal contraception
11. Frailty in elderly participants aged > 75 years, defined as: severe comorbidities associated with limited life expectancy; or Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) > 5; or cognitive impairment interfering with treatment adherence.
12. Inability to provide informed consent
13. History of diabetic ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar non ketotic coma
14. Concomitant anti-diabetic drugs other than metformin
15. Steroidal therapy within the last 3 months
16. Medications known to significantly impact glucose metabolism (e.g., atypical antipsychotics)
17. GAD-Ab positivity
18. Severe obesity (BMI > 40)
19. Altered levels of amylase and lipase
